original_interpretation: EU 2026 dual-use list update adds controls on semiconductor equipment/materials and advanced computing ICs; enters into force on OJ publication after 2-month scrutiny.
evidence_found: "Semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment and materials (e.g. Atomic Layer Deposition equipment for molybdenum and Ruthenium, ...)"; "Advanced computing integrated circuits (ICs) and electronic assemblies"; "The updated EU control list enters into force upon publication in the Official Journal after the usual two-month scrutiny period" (DG TRADE news, 14 Sep 2026)
notes: Adopted 14 Sep 2026 as a Delegated Regulation; as of 2026-10-01 still in the scrutiny window (not yet in force).

original_interpretation: EU dual-use list updates follow multilateral regime decisions incl. Wassenaar.
evidence_found: "The update brings the list in line with decisions taken in the multilateral Export Control Regime's Wassenaar Arrangement (WA), Australia Group (AG) and Nuclear Supplier Group (NSG) in 2025"; Annex I "is typically amended at least once each year via a Delegated Act based on decisions and commitments taken within the framework of the international non-proliferation regimes" (DG TRADE, 14 Sep 2026)

original_interpretation: Dec 2025 provisional agreement on revised EU FDI screening regulation; mandatory screening incl. semiconductors; applies 18 months after entry into force.
evidence_found: "all member states would establish screening mechanisms covering a targeted and clearly defined set of sensitive areas"; "hyper-critical technologies, such as artificial intelligence ..., quantum technologies and semiconductors"; "The new rules will start applying 18 months after the entry into force of the regulation." (Council press release, 11 Dec 2025)
notes: Accurate as a dated event. Status has moved on: adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1386 of 17 June 2026, published 26 June 2026, in force 16 July 2026, applies from 17 January 2028 (new claims added in this batch).

original_interpretation: Dutch amendment effective 1 April 2025 added measuring and inspection equipment to the national licence requirement.
evidence_found: "On 1 April 2025 the Netherlands will modify its national export control measure ... The new policy will apply, for example, to specific measuring and inspection equipment that can be used in the production of advanced semiconductors."; "This new authorisation requirement is the second time the national export control measure has been amended" (Government.nl, 15 Jan 2025)

original_interpretation: Japan added 23 types of SME to export controls for all destinations in July 2023.
evidence_found: "In July 2023 ... Japan strengthened export controls on advanced semiconductor-manufacturing equipment and added the export of 23 types of semiconductor-manufacturing equipment to all regions to the scope of control based on the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act." (METI White Paper 2024, Ch.2 Sec.2, Japan export control policy)

original_interpretation: Japan (Nov 2024) will provide 10 trillion yen+ public support to AI and semiconductors by FY2030.
evidence_found: "the Prime Minister announced yesterday that the government will provide public support of 10 trillion yen or more to the AI and semiconductor sectors by FY2030 and that it will formulate a new support framework to encourage public and private investment at the level of over 50 trillion yen" (METI Minister Muto press conference, 12 Nov 2024, Q&A)
notes: Announcement by PM Ishiba relayed by the METI minister; a policy target, not appropriated spending.

original_interpretation: Rapidus selected Nov 2025 as official operator, with a 100bn yen IPA investment, targeting 2nm mass production in 2027.
evidence_found: "Rapidus is planning to submit an application for investment of 100 billion yen by Japan's Information-technology Promotion Agency ... within the current fiscal year"; selection "based on the Japan act 'Promotion of Information Processing'"; "planned start of mass production of 2nm logic semiconductors in 2027" (Rapidus, 21 Nov 2025)
correction: On 21 Nov 2025 the 100bn yen IPA investment was only a planned application, not an investment made. It was completed by 27 Feb 2026 (267.6bn yen round incl. 100bn from IPA), and IPA added 150bn yen on 5 Jun 2026 (capital 424.95bn yen).
notes: Company self-report (reported_claim); new claims added for the 2026 rounds.

original_interpretation: Wassenaar: operational since 1996, 42 participating states, Dual-Use List implemented nationally, consensus decisions.
evidence_found: About us lists participating states (42 names, Argentina ... United States); "Participating States apply export controls to all items set forth in the List of Dual-Use Goods and Technologies"; "All measures ... are implemented on the basis of national discretion"; "All Plenary decisions are taken by consensus."; Origins: "first Plenary Meeting of the now operational Wassenaar Arrangement was held on 12-13 December 1996"
notes: 42 counted from the list on the page (last updated 17 Jun 2025).

original_interpretation: China required export licences for gallium and germanium from 1 Aug 2023.
evidence_found: "the Chinese government's announcement of new export controls on these critical minerals, effective August 1, 2023"; "Chinese export controls require export licenses for Chinese companies that meet the relevant requirements" (USITC EBOT, Mar 2024, pp.1-2)

original_interpretation: Per USITC, China produced ~60% of world germanium and close to 90% of gallium in 2022.
evidence_found: "China is the primary global producer of these minerals producing around 60 percent and close to 90 percent of the world's germanium and gallium in 2022, respectively." Footnote 2 cites Al Jazeera and Reuters (USITC EBOT, Mar 2024, p.1). USGS MCS 2026: "China accounted for 99% of worldwide primary low-purity gallium production."
correction: Attribution is accurate but the gallium share is dated and rests on press reports. Newer official data: USGS MCS 2026 puts China at 99% of world primary low-purity gallium production (see CLM-2249). Germanium share not re-checked.
notes: Contradiction record added (CLM-0345 vs CLM-2249). USITC EBOT reflects author views, per its disclaimer.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM Notice 2024 No.46 (3 Dec 2024) banned dual-use exports to US military users and in principle Ga/Ge/Sb/superhard exports to US.
evidence_found: "I. The export of dual-use items to U.S. military users or for military uses is prohibited. II. In principle, the export of the relevant dual-use items gallium, germanium, antimony, and superhard materials to the United States is not permitted"; "This notice is officially in force from the date on which it was promulgated." (CSET translation, MOFCOM, 3 Dec 2024)
notes: Clause II suspended 9 Nov 2025 to 27 Nov 2026 (CLM-0347). Source is a CSET translation of the MOFCOM text.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM Notice 2025 No.61 requires export permits for foreign-made items with >=0.1% value of Chinese-origin rare earths.
evidence_found: "contain, integrate, or have mixed in with them any rare earths listed in part 1 of Appendix 1 ... originally produced in China, such that the value of said rare earths comprises 0.1% or more of the value of said item" (CSET translation of MOFCOM Notice 2025 No. 61, announced 9 Oct 2025, para 1a)
notes: Suspended 7 Nov 2025 to 10 Nov 2026 by Announcement No. 70 (CLM-0349).

original_interpretation: China suspended the US-specific Ga/Ge/Sb/superhard ban (No.46 clause 2) from 9 Nov 2025 to 27 Nov 2026.
evidence_found: "The suspension of the second clause of the Announcement No. 46 of 2024 takes effect from Sunday until Nov. 27, 2026" (Xinhua, 9 Nov 2025). Pillsbury client alert concurs: "suspend Article 2 of Announcement No. 46 of 2024 from November 9, 2025, until November 27, 2026".
notes: Tier-3 state media; corroborated by Pillsbury Winthrop (law firm alert, opened this run, not added as a source). US-China truce extension to 10 Jan 2027 announced 23-24 Sep 2026 may shift this date; no Chinese announcement found.

original_interpretation: Announcement No.70 of 2025 suspended Nos. 55-58, 61, 62 from 7 Nov 2025 to 10 Nov 2026.
evidence_found: "On November 7, 2025, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the General Administration of Customs (GAC) jointly issued Announcement No. 70 of 2025, announcing the suspension of multiple previous announcements effective immediately until November 10, 2026. The suspended announcements include ... No. 55, 56, 57, and 58 of 2025, as well as MOFCOM Announcements No. 61 and 62" (CIRS Group)
notes: Tier-3; Pillsbury alert gives the same dates. Original MOFCOM text not read.

original_interpretation: Big Fund III registered May 2024, registered capital 344bn yuan, MoF led 19 state-owned investors.
evidence_found: "China is pumping another 344 billion yuan ($47.5 billion) into a state-backed semiconductor industry investment fund"; "The third phase of National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund has been set up with investments from 19 state-owned investors led by the Ministry of Finance, business registration records show." (Caixin Global, 28 May 2024)
correction: The readable (non-paywalled) text says the fund 'has been set up' with 344bn yuan of investments per registration records; it does not use the words 'registered capital' or give the registration date.
notes: Amount, investor count and MoF lead verified.

original_interpretation: 13 Sep 2025 MOFCOM anti-dumping probe on US analog ICs (interface, gate driver) and anti-discrimination probe.
evidence_found: "China launched two probes targeting the US semiconductor sector on Saturday"; "anti-dumping investigation into certain analog integrated circuits (ICs) imported from the US ... some commodity interface ICs and gate driver ICs"; "an anti-discrimination probe into US measures against China's chip sector" (Taipei Times, Mon 15 Sep 2025, p.9)
notes: 'Saturday' = 13 Sep 2025. Tier-3 (AP/Reuters copy).

original_interpretation: May 2023 CAC review: Micron posed security risks; CII operators to stop buying Micron.
evidence_found: "The review, which was conducted by China's Cybersecurity Review Office (CRO) on Micron's products sold in China, found that Micron's products negatively affect China's national security. As a result, the authorities demanded that China's domestic critical information infrastructure operators stop purchasing Micron products" (ECNS, 22 May 2023)
notes: Tier-3 state media relaying a CAC statement.

original_interpretation: Korea passed the Semiconductor Special Act 29 Jan 2026 without 52-hour exemption; expected effect Q3 2026.
evidence_found: "South Korea's National Assembly on Thursday passed ... the Special Act on Strengthening and Supporting the Competitiveness of the Semiconductor Industry"; "A clause that would have exempted semiconductor firms from the country's 52-hour workweek cap ... was removed"; "expected to take effect as early as the third quarter of this year" (Korea Herald, 29 Jan 2026)
notes: Expectation was met: the enforcement decree was approved 4 Aug 2026 and the Act took effect 11 Aug 2026 (new claim added).

original_interpretation: Feb 2025 K-Chips Act raised facility investment credit to 20% (large) and 30% (SMEs).
evidence_found: "the tax credit rate for conglomerates will rise to 20 percent from the current 15 percent, while the rate for small and medium-sized businesses will increase to 30 percent from 25 percent" (Korea Times, 27 Feb 2025)
notes: Applies to national strategic industries (semiconductors, secondary batteries, future cars), not chips only. Tier-3; statute not read.

original_interpretation: Taiwan Art.10-2: 25% R&D, 5% advanced equipment credit; thresholds NT$6bn R&D, 6% intensity, 12%/15% ETR; applications from Feb 2024.
evidence_found: "a 25% deduction for research and development expenses and a 5% deduction for expenditures on acquiring new eqipment for advanced processes"; "research and development expenses of at least NT$6 billion, a research and development density of 6%, and expenditures of NT$10 billion"; "effective tax rate of 12% for the fiscal year 112 and a threshold of 15% from the fiscal year 113"; applications "from February 1 to May 31" (TrendForce, 16 Jan 2024)
notes: Tier-2 relay of TechNews; statute text not read. Also requires NT$10bn advanced-equipment spend for the 5% credit.

original_interpretation: Jun 2025 Taiwan ITA added 601 entities incl. Huawei and SMIC to SHTC export control entity list.
evidence_found: DIGITIMES article body paywalled (headline only). Original ITA release (15 Jun 2025): "於本（6）月10日發布，新增俄羅斯、巴基斯坦、伊朗、緬甸、中國大陸涉及武擴活動等601個實體，其中亦包括華為、中芯等中資企業" (list updated 10 June: 601 entities added incl. Huawei and SMIC)
notes: Verified against the primary ITA press release (added as a source). List updated 10 Jun 2025, announced 15 Jun 2025; total then 10,844 entities.

original_interpretation: Semicon India programme approved Dec 2021 with Rs 76,000 crore; up to 50% fiscal support for fabs, compound semis, ATMP, design.
evidence_found: "the approval of India Semiconductor Mission 1.0 by the Union Cabinet in December 2021. The Mission is supported by an incentive framework of ₹76,000 crore, offering fiscal support of up to 50 per cent for silicon fabs, compound semiconductor facilities, assembly and testing units, and chip design." (PIB, ISM 2.0 backgrounder PDF, 7 Feb 2026, p.1)

original_interpretation: As of Dec 2025, 10 approved projects, Rs 1.60 lakh crore, 6 states.
evidence_found: "As of December 2025, 10 projects with a total investment of ₹1.60 lakh crore have been approved across 6 states." (PIB, ISM 2.0 backgrounder PDF, 7 Feb 2026, p.1)

original_interpretation: ISM 2.0 in Budget 2026-27 focusing on equipment/materials, Indian IP, supply chains; Rs 1,000 crore for FY2026-27.
evidence_found: "ISM 2.0 will focus on producing semiconductor equipment and materials in India, designing full stack Indian semiconductor intellectual property, and fortifying both domestic and global supply chains. A provision of Rs. 1,000 crore has been made for ISM 2.0 for FY 2026–27" (PIB, 7 Feb 2026, Introduction)
notes: Separately, the modified semiconductor and display programme has a 2026-27 outlay of ₹8,000 crore (same document).

original_interpretation: SEC reporters using 3TG necessary to products file annual Form SD by 31 May on DRC/adjoining-country origin.
evidence_found: "'necessary to the functionality or production of a product'"; "the term 'conflict minerals' includes tantalum, tin, gold, or tungsten"; "originated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo ('DRC') or an adjoining country"; "first Form SD filing on May 31, 2014 for the 2013 calendar year, and annually on May 31 for each calendar year thereafter" (SEC compliance guide)
notes: Page fetched with a declared user agent via shell (browser and web_extract got blocked or a fragment). The guide dates from the 2012 rule; later SEC staff positions on the Conflict Minerals Report were not checked.

original_interpretation: SEMI Standards: voluntary consensus technical agreements, >5,000 technologists, worldwide ballot.
evidence_found: "SEMI Standards are voluntary technical agreements for the semiconductor, flat panel display, ... industries."; "Over 5,000 technologists worldwide, representing all levels of the supply chain"; "it will initiate a worldwide balloting process to confirm that the document has global consensus"; "Use of SEMI standards is entirely voluntary" (SEMI, About SEMI Standards)
notes: The /en page body was partly blocked (Cloudflare); full text read on SEMI's /cn copy of the same page (English text). Self-description (reported_claim).

original_interpretation: SEMI Standards topic areas list.
evidence_found: "SEMI Standards cover many topics related to electronics manufacturing: 3D-IC, Equipment Automation (Hardware and Software), Flat-Panel Displays, Facilities, Gases, High Brightness-LED, MEMS/NEMS, Materials, Microlithography, Packaging, Photovoltaic, Process Chemicals, Silicon Material & Process Control, and Traceability." (SEMI, About SEMI Standards)
notes: SEMI's own description; arguably reported_claim rather than fact, but it is just a scope list.

original_interpretation: JEDEC (1958) develops open standards incl. DDR, HBM, LPDDR, flash, packaging, ESD; >380 member companies.
evidence_found: About: "JEDEC is the global leader in developing open standards for the microelectronics industry, with more than 3,000 volunteers representing over 380 member companies."; "Since 1958, JEDEC has earned a reputation ...". Home: focus areas "Main Memory: DDR SDRAM, HBM", "Flash Memory", "Low Power Memory: LPDDR", "ESD: Electrostatic Discharge"; committees cover "quality & reliability, and packaging"
notes: 'Founded in 1958' follows the page's 'Since 1958'; the body traces to JETEC (1944) and took the JEDEC name in 1958. Self-description.

original_interpretation: CHIPS incentives moved from grant-only awards toward negotiated deals with government equity after 2025.
evidence_found: EO 14255 (31 Mar 2025): Investment Accelerator "shall be responsible for the CHIPS Program Office ..., which shall focus on ... negotiating much better deals than those of the previous administration." Intel 8-K: "U.S. Government to make $8.9 billion investment in Intel common stock". NIST (29 Jul 2026): "The Department will receive a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each company as a condition for receiving the funds"
notes: Reasoning follows from CLM-0316 and CLM-0317, and later evidence makes it stronger: CHIPS R&D letters of intent from 2026 make equity a stated condition (new claim added).

original_interpretation: Taxonomy of semiconductor regulation into 8 clusters across jurisdictions.
evidence_found: Checked against the batch's claims: export controls (US/NL/JP/TW/EU/CN) and subsidies (US/EU/JP/KR/TW/IN/CN incl. Big Fund) hold; tariffs/remedies (US 232/301, CN anti-dumping) hold; FDI/outbound screening, CN mineral controls, CN cybersecurity review (Micron), US conflict minerals and SEMI/JEDEC standards hold. EU F-gas/PFAS rest on CLM-0334/CLM-0335, which are 'unknown' claims.
correction: The 'environmental/chemical (EU F-gas/PFAS)' cluster isn't evidenced: CLM-0334 and CLM-0335 could not establish how these rules treat semiconductor uses.
notes: Interpretation; no source required.

original_interpretation: Mapping of instruments to affected participants (designers, SME makers, HBM makers, China fabs, US persons; subsidies to fab operators; minerals to materials suppliers).
evidence_found: Consistent with CLM-0302 (US-person licence), CLM-0304 (SME FDP rules, HBM 3A090.c), CLM-0307 (AI chips). But subsidies are broader than fabs: Taiwan Art.10-2 targets R&D-heavy firms incl. fabless (CLM-0356), India ISM covers chip design (CLM-0358), and CHIPS R&D letters of intent fund photonics/memory/packaging firms (NIST, 29 Jul 2026).
correction: 'Subsidies mainly affect fab operators' is too narrow: R&D tax credits, design-linked incentives and CHIPS R&D awards also reach fabless designers, packaging and materials firms.
notes: Interpretation; export-control and mineral parts follow from the cited claims.

original_interpretation: Many 2025-26 measures are suspended or have scheduled step-ups (affiliates rule to Nov 2026, China mineral bans to Nov 2026, Section 301 step-up June 2027), so need dated re-checks.
evidence_found: FR 2025-19846: "The suspension is set to end November 9, 2026, absent a future extension."; Xinhua: suspension "until Nov. 27, 2026"; CIRS: "until November 10, 2026"; FR 2025-23912 Annex: rate "shall be increased on June 23, 2027". Crowell (Sep 2026): truce extended to 10 Jan 2027; "BIS has not yet published a Federal Register notice formally extending the suspension"
notes: The inference holds and later evidence makes it stronger: the 23-24 Sep 2026 truce extension to 10 Jan 2027 is expected to move the Nov 2026 dates (see CLM-2257/2258), which shows exactly why these need dated re-checks.
